_doc: X KOL collector config. Exploration layer — output NEVER enters investment_protocol decisions (buy_threshold / position_size / verdict). Roster is curated by hand; no agent may auto-add accounts.

budget._doc: Hard ceiling in USD. The collector refuses to issue a request once the projected worst-case spend would cross total_usd. Prices are X pay-per-use as of 2026-08; update both if X changes them.

pacing._doc: Single-threaded, fixed spacing. min_interval_sec is the floor between any two HTTP calls; a 429 backs off to backoff_sec and doubles up to backoff_max_sec. Measured 2026-08-06 on the free syndication endpoint: ~8 rapid requests triggered 429 with a ~183s cooldown, so the same queue-don't-burst discipline is applied here.

collect._doc: max_results is a CEILING, not a promise — asking 10 returned 5 (observed 2026-08-06). Billing is per resource RETURNED, so raising it costs nothing when the account is quiet; it only widens the window that a single page can cover. 100 is the API maximum. max_pages_per_sweep bounds next_token pagination, which exists to stop a busy account's posts falling into a silent gap below the watermark. first_run_max caps the cold-start backfill (that one does NOT paginate — Serenity alone has 6,000+ posts of history).

heat._doc: Theme-heat weights, hand-calibrated like the rest of the exploration layer — no agent may auto-tune them. primary vs secondary: validated 2026-08-06 on real data — in a joke about how to pronounce $AAOI, the props $TSM/$AMD tracked the market (+4.8%/+1.4% 5d) while the subject $AAOI ran +45.8%. So position matters, but secondary mentions are NOT noise ($SIVE surfaced only as a secondary and was the actual supply-chain link), hence a reduced weight rather than zero.
